body: Large Language Models are increasingly deployed in public-sector settings, where incorrect guidance can cause irreversible harm. We introduce CIVI, the first framework for diagnosing search agent failures in civic information. Its benchmark instantiation jointly spans cross-national, interjurisdictional government contexts (federal, state, and local) and functional categories from an internationally adopted United Nations standard. We evaluate ten frontier search agents and find that none matches an attentive human baseline. Alongside accuracy, CIVI measures search invocation rate, selective no-search accuracy, and how often agents cite authoritative government sources. To perform this diagnosis, we introduce ARISE, which decomposes agentic search failures into four mutually exclusive modes, isolated via source-injection ablation. ARISE attributes 72.1% of all observed failures to retrieval-bound causes rather than to gaps in the models' parametric knowledge.
summaryZh: 该研究介绍了CIVI（Civic Information Search Agent Failure Diagnosis Framework），这是首个用于诊断公共服务领域搜索智能体失败的框架。其基准测试涵盖了跨国、跨司法管辖区的政府背景和联合国标准的功能类别。研究评估了十个前沿搜索智能体，发现均未达到人类基线水平。CIVI不仅衡量准确率，还评估搜索调用率、选择性无搜索准确率以及引用权威来源的频率。为实现诊断，研究引入了ARISE方法，将智能体搜索失败分解为四种互斥模式，并发现72.1%的失败源于检索限制而非模型参数知识的不足。
